_comment: Credentials for the mobile-app link association files served from
/.well-known/ (see scripts/emit-well-known.mjs).
READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING IT. Until 2026-09-05 this file was empty and the
emitter wrote nothing, and the assetlinks.json served at indigenworld.com
was **generated by Firebase Hosting itself** from the Android apps
registered in the Firebase project. That is why it kept reappearing after
deploys and why nothing in this repo produced it: it was never a deployed
file. Its response carries none of the headers firebase.json sets for
/.well-known/assetlinks.json, which is how you can tell the two apart.
The entries below reproduce that generated file exactly, with one addition:
delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds on the production package. That
relation is what lets the app hold a credential scoped to this domain - the
restore key behind Zero-Tap Sign-In, required by Google Play from April
2027 - and Firebase cannot be asked to include it. Serving our own file is
the only way to claim it.
THE TRADE: a file served from here **overrides** the generated one. Firebase
no longer fills in the gaps, so a new Android app, a new flavour or a
rotated signing key must be added below by hand or App Links silently stop
verifying for it. That is the cost of the relation above.
Nothing here is a secret. A SHA-256 signing fingerprint is public by design
- it is what every device checks the association against - and all four
below were already being served publicly.
WHERE THE FINGERPRINTS COME FROM:
- Play App Signing: Play Console > Test and release > Setup > App signing
> App signing key certificate > SHA-256.
- Upload and local release keys: cd apps/mobile/android && ./gradlew :app:signingReport
Uppercase, colon-separated, exactly as reported.
An empty android list means neither file is generated and neither is
deployed, which restores Firebase automatic behaviour. That is the safe
fallback and it is deliberate: a malformed association file makes Android
cache a verification failure, and no link opens the app until it expires.
